t.1.17.1: When that horse sacrifice, the rite of the great-souled one, had been completed, the gods received their shares and returned the way they had come.
t.1.17.2: Having completed the observances of his consecration, the king, accompanied by the company of his wives and attended by his servants, troops and vehicles, entered the city.
t.1.17.3: The lords of the earth, honored by that king as befitted them, bowed to the foremost of sages and departed joyfully for their own lands.
t.1.17.4: When the lords of the earth had departed, the glorious King Daśaratha entered the city once more, placing the foremost of the twice-born at his head.
t.1.17.5: Then Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, well honored, set out together with Śāntā, followed by the wise king along with his retinue.
t.1.17.7: Kausalyā shone with that son of boundless splendour, just as Aditi shone with the thunderbolt-wielding Vajrapāṇi, the foremost of the gods.
t.1.17.6: Kausalyā bore Rāma, endowed with divine marks, a son of great fortune, half of Viṣṇu, the delight of the Ikṣvākus.
t.1.17.8: Of Kaikeyī was born the one named Bharata, whose valor was true, a fourth part of Viṣṇu himself, endowed with all virtues.
t.1.17.9: Then Sumitrā gave birth to two sons, Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, heroes skilled in all weapons, each endowed with a half of Viṣṇu's portion.
t.1.17.10: Four great-souled sons were born, each in turn, to the king, virtuous and worthy of him, and in their radiance they were like the stars of Proṣṭhapada.
t.1.17.11: When the eleventh day had passed, he performed the naming ceremony: the eldest, the great-souled Rāma, and Bharata, the son of Kaikayī.
t.1.17.12: Then Vasiṣṭha, supremely pleased, bestowed the names, calling one son of Sumitrā Lakṣmaṇa and likewise the other Śatrughna. He had all the rites performed for them, beginning with the birth ceremonies.
t.1.17.13: Among them the eldest, Rāma, was like a banner, a source of delight to his father, and, like the Self-born Svayambhū, he was held in high esteem by all beings.
t.1.17.14: All of them were knowers of the Vedas and valiant; all were devoted to the welfare of the world. All were endowed with knowledge, and all were richly furnished with virtues.
t.1.17.15: Among them, too, was Rāma, of great splendor and true valor; and Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of good fortune, was deeply affectionate from his very childhood.
t.1.17.17: Lakṣmaṇa, endowed with good fortune, was like a second life-breath outside his body; without him the best of men could not find sleep, nor would he eat the fine food brought to him unless Lakṣmaṇa was with him.
t.1.17.16: He always did everything that was pleasing to Rāma, his eldest brother, the delight of the world, even at the cost of his own body.
t.1.17.18: Whenever Rāghava, mounted on a horse, goes out hunting, he follows close behind him with his bow, guarding him.
t.1.17.20: Daśaratha, with his four illustrious and beloved sons, became supremely delighted, like the Grandsire surrounded by the gods.
t.1.17.19: Likewise, Śatrughna, the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, was always dearer than life itself to Bharata, and Bharata was just as dear to him.
t.1.17.22: Then King Daśaratha, whose soul was devoted to dharma, together with his preceptors and kinsmen, began to consider the matter of their marriage.
t.1.17.21: When they had all grown endowed with knowledge and rich in virtues, modest and renowned, all-knowing and far-seeing,
t.1.17.24: Desiring to see the king, he said to the gatekeepers: "Announce quickly that I, Kauśika, the son of Gādhi, have arrived."
t.1.17.23: While that great-souled one was deliberating in the midst of his ministers, O mighty and radiant one, the great sage Viśvāmitra arrived.
t.1.17.25: Hearing those words of his, they all ran to the royal palace, their minds agitated, urged on by that speech.
t.1.17.26: Then, having gone to the royal palace, they announced to the Ikṣvāku king that the sage Viśvāmitra had arrived.
t.1.17.28: Seeing the ascetic of rigorous vows blazing with radiance, the king, his face beaming with joy, then had the guest-offering brought.
t.1.17.27: Having heard those words of theirs, he, composed and accompanied by his family priest, went forth in delight to meet him, just as Vāsava goes forth to meet Brahmā.
t.1.17.29: Having received the arghya offering from the king in the manner laid down in the scriptures, he asked the lord of men about his welfare and his undiminished prosperity.
t.1.17.30: Having met Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of sages asked after his well-being, and likewise, as was proper, inquired after the welfare of those illustrious ṛṣis.
t.1.17.31: All of them, with joyful hearts, entered the palace of that king; honored there, they sat down in a fitting manner.
t.1.17.32: Then the king, glad of heart and supremely noble, joyfully honoring the great sage Viśvāmitra, spoke to him.
t.1.17.33: Like the attainment of nectar, like rain in a waterless land, like the birth of a son by a worthy wife to one who is childless, like the recovery of what was lost, like the joy at a great rise of fortune...
t.1.17.34: And what supreme wish of yours shall I, overjoyed, fulfill? You are a worthy recipient of my gifts, O brahmin; by good fortune you have come, O righteous one. Today my birth has borne fruit, and my life has been well lived.
t.1.17.35: Formerly known by the title of royal sage, your splendor made radiant by austerity, you have attained the status of a brahmarṣi; you are worthy of honor from me in many ways.
t.1.17.36: This is a wonder, O brahmin, supremely purifying for me; and through the sight of you, O lord, it is as though I have come to an auspicious holy place.
t.1.17.37: Tell me what task you seek to have done, the purpose of your coming here. Favored as I am, I wish to further your purpose.
t.1.17.38: You ought not to feel any hesitation about the task, O Kauśika; I shall accomplish it entirely, for you are a deity to me.
t.1.17.39: Hearing these words, delightful to the heart and pleasing to the ear, spoken with modesty by that self-possessed king, the supreme sage, whose virtues and fame were renowned and who was distinguished by his virtues, attained the highest joy.
